transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-05-15 14:00 UTC
- Duration: ~65 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood CSM); Marta Ruiz (VentoCare Procurement), Anand Patel (VentoCare Infosec), Karen O'Neal (VentoCare Legal), Dexter Lin (VentoCare Platform), Simon Wu (VentoCare Privacy)

Auto-summary (auto):
- Purpose: align procurement, legal, and infosec on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA targets, and technical requirements for a pilot.
- Key asks from VentoCare: customer-managed keys (BYOK/HSM), EU data residency for PHI-derived telemetry, SOC2 Type II evidence, explicit SLA on availability and incident response windows, and clear egress/costing guidance.
- Agreed pilot: 6-week pilot, Redwood to run a performance benchmark; outcome will inform Dedicated vs Private decision.

Topics: MSA redlines, DPA obligations, SLA availability and credits, KMS/BYOK, SSO/SAML, audit artifacts, pilot scope and acceptance criteria, pricing commit/commitment term.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everybody, thanks for making time. we're going to run through the MSA redline asks, DPA constraints, and then Priya will walk through the private deployment options and KMS stuff. sound good?
[00:08] Marta Ruiz: yep, that's great. quick note, we have procurement deadlines for the end of June so we need clarity on commercial path and any blockers.
[00:14] Jordan Lee: totally. i'll try to keep the legal/commercial bits concise — then deep dive.
[00:18] Karen O'Neal: before we start, two items from legal: indemnity cap conversation and data residency guarantees. we need to be explicit in the DPA for any patient-derived content.
[00:27] Jordan Lee: understoood. we can mark those as high-priority redlines. our standard MSA has limits but we can propose alternate language; i'll send an annotated copy after this call.
[00:36] Anand Patel: on infosec side, our blocking items are BYOK for encryption in flight and at rest, SOC2 Type II evidence, and an ability to schedule a pentest window. also, we want audit logs that do not leave EU nodes when processing EU data.
[00:51] Priya Nair: quick clarification - for BYOK we support customer-managed keys via KMS integration; there are two options: cloud-KMS with redwood-managed wrapper, or a dedicated HSM in a private deployment. the second is available for Private/VPC deployments.
[01:06] Dexter Lin: can you explain the tradeoffs — performance/latency vs cost — between hosted with KMS vs private HSM?
[01:12] Priya Nair: yes. hosted + cloud-KMS is lowest ops and cost; latency is minimal for most workloads, but for PHI or regulated throughput we recommend Private with co-located HSM to keep keys in-customer control and reduce cross-region egress. HSM adds complexity and an up-front set-up and monthly fee.
[01:30] Marta Ruiz: what about egress costs? our finance team is sensitive to unpredictable egress fees, especially for embedding pipelines.
[01:36] Jordan Lee: good point. we can provide a cost model — Redwood Optimize gives batching and caching suggestions to reduce token egress. for pilot we can run a cost projection spreadsheet (we have a template) — i'll attach after the call. link: https://app.redwood.ai/pilot-cost-template (note: internal link)
[01:54] Karen O'Neal: returning to the MSA - we have a standard 60-day review window; exceptions on warranty, liability, and data residency must be clearly enumerated. also, termination for convenience notice period — we prefer 90 days commercial, is that negotiable?
[02:08] Jordan Lee: our standard is 30 days, but for enterprise we can take 60; 90 is higher than we typically accept but we can sketch options tied to committed volume. we should capture that as a pricing & term negotiation item.
[02:21] Simon Wu: also, can you confirm that logs and telemetry used for quality monitoring can be disabled or kept in customer-only storage? we need strict controls for PHI-derived signals.
[02:31] Priya Nair: yes, we have per-customer telemetry toggles. for Private deployments we can keep telemetry in-customer and redact or route to customer KMS. for hosted, we have scoping options to limit retention and pseudonymize.
[02:44] Anand Patel: about the SLA, we need >99.9% availability for inference endpoints and an Incident Response MTTx guarantee; also credits calculation in case of missed SLOs. can you share your standard SLA wording?
[02:58] Jordan Lee: we have a standard SLA doc; for Dedicated/Private we offer higher availability tiers and a financial credit schedule. i'll attach the SLA matrix. Priya, can you call out technical mechanisms that ensure low latency and high availability?
[03:12] Priya Nair: sure — runtime features: multi-region routing, automatic fallback to compatible model variants, continuous batching to keep latency under SLOs, and KV cache warmup for repeated sessions. for Dedicated we reserve capacity which avoids noisy neighbor issues.
[03:27] (Some cross talk)
[03:34] Marta Ruiz: procurement - timeline wise, if we want to sign in June, what's the sequence?
[03:38] Jordan Lee: sequence we typically use: 1) Legal & Procurement redline MSA/DPA in parallel, 2) Technical pilot (6 weeks) to validate perf and cost, 3) Final commercial terms (commit or reserved capacity), 4) Onboarding/rollout. we can compress but need approvals.
[03:52] Karen O'Neal: can we get a draft DPA that includes the EU data residency clause and the right-to-audit language?
[03:58] Jordan Lee: yes, we'll include an appendix for EU data residency and a right-to-audit clause aligned to industry norms. i'll flag the DPA redlines in the annotated bundle.
[04:07] Dexter Lin: about the pilot: what environment will it run in? hosted or dedicated?
[04:11] Priya Nair: pilot can run in Redwood Hosted with dataset partitioning to EU region and with telemetry toggles on. if you prefer Private pilot, that's possible but will add provisioning time. usually we do a hosted pilot to move faster.
[04:26] Anand Patel: we are wary of hosted for PHI. if it's PHI-adjacent we need Private or at least strict pseudonymization and customer keys.
[04:34] Jordan Lee: understood, we can scope the pilot around synthetic or de-identified data for initial perf; next step would be a gated test with PHI in Private.
[04:43] Simon Wu: what's the expected timeline to provision a Private environment with HSM?
[04:47] Priya Nair: typically 3-6 weeks depending on networking and KMS integrations. we can accelerate with a checklist.
[04:55] Marta Ruiz: procurement question — we need clarity on price breaks for 12 vs 24 month commitments and what happens if usage is lower than committed.
[05:02] Jordan Lee: we offer tiered committed pricing. lower actual usage typically triggers reconciliation — we can propose a true-up model or credits. i'll include a pricing worksheet for the pilot.
[05:14] Karen O'Neal: indemnity - our counsel wants a mutual indemnity for IP claims and an exception carveout for data breaches attributable to Redwood. also, limitation of liability to be defined; we cannot accept extremely low caps for PHI exposures.
[05:29] Jordan Lee: we can propose a higher cap for PHI-related liabilities and an insurance representation. that's something for legal redlines.
[05:36] Anand Patel: also need to clarify SOC2 report periodicity and a current pen-test summary. can Redwood provide whitepapers or attestations?
[05:44] Jordan Lee: yes, we have SOC2 Type II report and pen-test summary. i'll send those to Anand and Simon after getting an NDA or secure link. we can also provide architecture review sessions.
[05:55] Priya Nair: technical note — our runtime can be configured to pin model versions and do canary rollouts; that helps with regression control during pilot.
[06:05] Dexter Lin: good. will Redwood support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for provisioning?
[06:10] Priya Nair: yes, SAML and SCIM supported for both Hosted and Dedicated. for Private we can integrate in your IdP via SAML.
[06:18] Marta Ruiz: Finance will also want an escrow or assurance that committed funds map to deliverables; is there a standard milestone schedule?
[06:25] Jordan Lee: we usually map committed capacity to billing schedule and have milestone credits for rollout. we can surface options and a milestone-based pay schedule if that helps.
[06:34] Karen O'Neal: one more legal item — export controls and data transfer clauses, specifically EEA <-> US transfer. we need clarity on lawful transfer mechanisms (SCCs or equivalent).
[06:44] Jordan Lee: we'll include standard SCC language and can work with your privacy counsel on the specific annexes.
[06:50] (short pause)
[07:00] Jordan Lee: ok, let's do a quick recap and next steps. action items: priy a will share the private deployment diagram and KMS options; i'll send annotated MSA and DPA with EU appendix; liam will set up pilot workspace; karen and anand will provide required legal & infosec evidence.
[07:18] Karen O'Neal: i'll circulate high level redlines by 2026-05-22.
[07:23] Anand Patel: i'll share a list of infosec artifacts and a preferred pentest window by 2026-05-22.
[07:29] Marta Ruiz: procurement will review pricing worksheet once received and aim to decide on path to commit by late June.
[07:35] Jordan Lee: perfect. i'll follow up with a single bundle (MSA+DPA+SLA+pricing) and a suggested pilot plan.
[07:42] Liam O'Connor: i'll invite the VentoCare platform team to the pilot workspace and schedule the benchmark run for week of 2026-05-25.
[07:50] (some small talk)
[07:55] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity — we'll keep the channel open and follow up with the doc bundle.
[08:00] Marta Ruiz: thanks, bye.

Notes / references shared on call:
- Pilot cost template: https://app.redwood.ai/pilot-cost-template
- Annotated MSA/DPA (to be sent by Jordan): will include EU appendix and indemnity options
- Private deployment diagram (Priya to share): includes BYOK/HSM paths and expected provisioning timeline
- SLA matrix (Jordan to attach)

End of transcript.
